== Midtones contrast ==

James Popsys as a general rule suggest to reduce the contrast in the mid-tones 

From Claude:

In darktable, the closest equivalent to Lightroom's Clarity adjustment would be the "local contrast" module (sometimes called "local contrast enhancement" in older versions).
This module operates similarly to Clarity by enhancing mid-tone contrast.
However, you have a few options in darktable that can achieve similar effects:

- The primary equivalent is the "local contrast" module found in the tone group
- You can also use the "contrast equalizer" module, which gives you more fine-grained control over contrast adjustments at different detail scales
- The "diffuse or sharpen" module (introduced in newer versions) can also be used to achieve similar effects

The "local contrast" module is generally the most straightforward replacement for Lightroom's Clarity.
Like Clarity, it enhances local contrast while avoiding the stronger haloing effects that can occur with traditional sharpening methods.


= Highlights vs Shadows =

When taking a photo, try to not blow the highlights, try keeping as much detail as possible.
In post-processing, generally, a histogram with some shadow is good and helps to avoid the photo looking overexposed.

== Luminance ==

Favour luminance over than saturation and hue to bring up the color.
